specificity.question: Which side expresses a coherent direction derived from this product and its user jobs?
specificity.preferenceFor: Prefer the side whose visual choices and signature move are meaningfully tied to the supplied product intent instead of interchangeable novelty.
specificity.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides are equally product-specific or equally detached from the brief.
specificity.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when the supplied captures do not expose enough of the product direction.
evidenceRequirements: Name a visible decision and connect it to a declared user job.
Distinguish product fit from novelty or decorative difference.

hierarchy.question: Which side makes the primary job, state, and next action easier to understand and scan?
hierarchy.preferenceFor: Prefer the side with clearer ordering, grouping, emphasis, and density rhythm across every supplied state without flattening all content into equal cards.
hierarchy.tieWhen: Use tie when the sides provide materially equivalent scan order and information priority.
hierarchy.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when the primary content or required state is absent from both capture sets.
evidenceRequirements: Identify what reads first and why in at least one capture.
Cite grouping, emphasis, or density behavior rather than personal taste alone.

uxCorrectness.question: Which side better preserves the declared jobs, content truth, states, and protected capabilities?
uxCorrectness.preferenceFor: Prefer the side that keeps required actions discoverable, represents state truthfully, avoids fabricated content, and does not sacrifice product behavior for visual cleanliness.
uxCorrectness.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides preserve or violate the visible UX contract to the same degree.
uxCorrectness.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable for behavior that cannot be inferred from the captured states; screenshots alone do not prove interaction execution.
evidenceRequirements: Cite a protected capability, state, or content-truth requirement.
Limit conclusions to what the supplied captures actually demonstrate.

uiDnaPreservation.question: Which side better preserves the declared project DNA while making purposeful improvements?
uiDnaPreservation.preferenceFor: Prefer the side that retains recognizable typography, color, spacing, surface, component, imagery, and motion posture or makes a clearly beneficial intentional departure.
uiDnaPreservation.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides preserve the declared DNA equally well or depart from it equally without purpose.
uiDnaPreservation.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when the fixture has no relevant DNA declaration for the visible captures.
evidenceRequirements: Reference at least one declared DNA role and one visible implementation detail.
Do not treat pixel similarity or preservation of an existing flaw as the goal.

responsiveness.question: Which side adapts its hierarchy and controls more successfully across the required viewports?
responsiveness.preferenceFor: Prefer genuine reflow and reprioritization without clipping, shrink-only scaling, lost actions, unreadable density, or viewport-specific dead space.
responsiveness.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides adapt equally well or exhibit equivalent responsive defects.
responsiveness.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when matched content is not shown at more than one required viewport.
evidenceRequirements: Compare the same job or state across at least two viewport captures.
Cite reflow, action placement, clipping, density, or readable sizing.

genericness.question: Which side is less generic and less dependent on interchangeable AI-interface conventions?
genericness.preferenceFor: Prefer the more restrained and product-specific side, with fewer unjustified card grids, pills, gradients, icon decoration, generic slogans, or dashboard cliches.
genericness.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides are equally distinctive or equally generic after accounting for product fit.
genericness.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when the captures are too narrow to distinguish a system from a single isolated component.
evidenceRequirements: Name the visible convention or distinctive move being compared.
Do not reward novelty that damages usability, hierarchy, or product fit.

productHierarchyFidelity.question: Which side keeps the declared primary product object central while treating supporting objects and execution mechanisms as subordinate?
productHierarchyFidelity.preferenceFor: Prefer the side whose navigation, page titles, visual weight, and task flow preserve the fixture's primary-object hierarchy instead of promoting a downstream tool, artifact, or execution mechanism into the product's center.
productHierarchyFidelity.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides preserve the hierarchy equally well or drift from it to the same material degree.
productHierarchyFidelity.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when the fixture declares no productHierarchy context or the supplied captures do not show the primary and competing objects.
evidenceRequirements: Name the declared primary object and identify where the visible hierarchy places it.
Cite one supporting object or execution mechanism and explain whether its visual weight is appropriately subordinate.

shellContinuity.question: Which side preserves the accepted product shell and route context across the supplied surfaces?
shellContinuity.preferenceFor: Prefer the side that retains the declared global navigation, project context, breadcrumbs, typography roles, and shell geometry while allowing each nested module to express its own job without looking like a separate product.
shellContinuity.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides preserve or break the declared shell invariants to an equivalent degree.
shellContinuity.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when no shellContinuity context is declared or fewer than two captures expose the shared shell.
evidenceRequirements: Compare the same declared shell invariant in at least two captures.
Separate shell continuity from incidental pixel matching or repeated content layout.

referenceScopeFidelity.question: Which side uses each supplied reference only within its declared role and scope?
referenceScopeFidelity.preferenceFor: Prefer the side that applies allowed functional, stylistic, anchor, or edit-target influence without importing forbidden shell, brand, copy, hierarchy, or component decisions from that reference.
referenceScopeFidelity.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides respect or violate the declared reference boundaries to the same extent.
referenceScopeFidelity.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when no scoped reference is declared or the referenced feature is not visible in the supplied captures.
evidenceRequirements: Name the reference role and one allowed influence visible in the result.
Check at least one declared forbidden influence instead of judging resemblance in the abstract.

capabilityFit.question: Which side expresses the declared complex capability with the most suitable, accessible, and product-consistent interaction primitive?
capabilityFit.preferenceFor: Prefer the side whose visible primitive, controls, density, selection model, and required fallback fit the declared capability and project constraints without creating an ornamental custom interaction system.
capabilityFit.tieWhen: Use tie when both sides provide materially equivalent capability fit and fallbacks or expose equivalent mismatches.
capabilityFit.notJudgeableWhen: Use not-judgeable when no capabilityFit context is declared, the relevant primitive or fallback is absent, or the conclusion would require invisible library-comparison or implementation-provenance evidence.
evidenceRequirements: Cite a visible capability requirement and how the chosen primitive supports or obstructs it.
Verify the declared fallback or mark the dimension not-judgeable; do not infer library evaluation from pixels.
